newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu decides to keep Israeli justice minister.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu decides to keep Israeli justice minister.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has decided against sacking his justice minister over a corruption scandal that will go to the High Court this week, a spokeswoman said on Sunday.
"The prime minister has decided after weighing the various aspects of this affair to leave Tzachi Hanegbi in his post," said a justice ministry spokeswoman.

State prosecutors said after a police probe last month there were "real suspicions" of corruption and breach of trust by Netanyahu and Hangebi in the short-lived appointment in January of an attorney-general. But they did not indict the two, citing lack of evidence.

The spokeswoman said Netanyahu's decision not to sack Hanegbi was contained in a written state response to petitions asking the High Court to order indictments against Netanyahu, Hanegbi and a key Netanyahu aide.
The petitions will be heard in court on Wednesday.
The results of the three-month police probe prompted members of Netanyahu's own government to call for Hanegbi's dismissal.
"He (Netanyahu) decided Hanegbi is worthy of his post," the spokeswoman said.

Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky said last month he would take his party's seven seats out of the coalition, denying Netanyahu his 66-54 parliamentary majority, if unspecified changes were not made in the government.

A Channel One television report spurred the inquiry into the appointment of Likud activist and lawyer Roni Bar-On in January. It alleged key coalition member Aryeh Deri pressed Netanyahu to appoint Bar-On, who would offer him a plea bargain in an ongoing corruption trial.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry that he was unqualified for the job.
